A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PILOT and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A–G, and case studies. Added content and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning and code-generation experiments, component ablations, latency measurements, and appendix analyses of teacher capability, training data, and cross-domain transfer.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds textual-planning comparisons and representation-isotropy measurements in Section 5.3.

M1.justification: PILOT’s data construction, context aggregation, Hyper-Network, prototype modulation, energy-aligned injection, and two-phase optimization remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix F. The new textual-planning procedures are comparison methods.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MATH and MBPP and evaluate on MATH500, AIMO, GSM8K, HumanEval, and MBPP. The new controls use existing benchmarks; the appendix cross-domain transfer scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: New Table 3 adds External Planning Prompting using DeepSeek-V3.1 hints at inference and LoRA SFT (Text Distillation), which learns to emit heuristic guidance. These introduce direct alternatives to latent planning across five benchmarks on Qwen2.5-7B, substantially expanding the central comparison. Table 1’s original comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds protocols for answer-blind teacher hints and textual distillation using the existing 543 math and 267 code training examples. A new diagnostic measures average pairwise cosine similarity of final-layer, last-generated-token states over 100 correctly solved examples per domain. Existing experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds targeted checks of whether explicit textual planning reproduces PILOT’s gains and whether latent injection causes representation collapse. Existing component ablations, energy and depth analyses, teacher sensitivity, data-scale comparisons, cross-domain tests, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The existing five-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and Figure 5’s standard-deviation shading remain unchanged. New Tables 3–4 provide point estimates without introducing new run counts, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests; the diagnostic’s N=100 specifies its sample size.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. New Table 3 reports MATH500 scores of 72.60 for external planning and 72.20 for textual distillation versus PILOT’s retained 75.24; external planning leads on GSM8K, 89.31 versus 89.17. New Table 4 reports cosine similarities decreasing from 0.838 to 0.692 for math and 0.944 to 0.867 for code.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), mathematical definitions, optimization objectives, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged in substance. The new cosine-similarity diagnostic is an empirical measurement; no theorem, proof, or formal derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims of non-invasive, query-conditioned latent planning, improved math and coding performance, and minimal inference overhead. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 introduces a text-serialization bottleneck and exposure-bias explanation for textual planning’s weaker results. It also interprets lower pairwise cosine similarity as evidence against oversmoothing and in favor of preserving representation geometry. Section 7’s stated limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a PILOT code-repository link. Section 5.3 documents the new comparators’ teacher, hint construction, and shared training subset sizes. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters in Appendices F–G remain unchanged; repository availability is not independently established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 removes seven references, including DUET, HealthGPT, VideoRefer, PixelRefer, and BoostMIS, and deletes the introduction’s associated analogies to adaptation and vision tasks. The main related-work discussion of reasoning, adaptation, and activation steering remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Section 5.3, shortens an introductory positioning paragraph, and updates author affiliations to include Shanghai AI Laboratory. The remaining narrative and appendix organization are largely retained, with subsequent subsection and table renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3–4, enlarges Figure 5 and expands its caption heading, and reflows existing figures, tables, and equations. Existing graphical content is retained, and the three case-study pages are visually identical after relocation.

improvement.justification: The new textual-planning controls and representation diagnostic provide useful additional support for PILOT, while the code link improves access information. The gains are limited: external planning slightly exceeds PILOT on GSM8K, and cosine measurements on correctly solved examples do not fully establish geometry preservation or the proposed causal explanation for textual planning’s shortcomings.
